back: A series of equal payments made at regular intervals (monthly, quarterly, etc.).
Examples: mortgage payments, insurance premiums, lottery payouts.
Can be ordinary (end of period) or annuity due (beginning).
Payments are made at the [[imp:end of each period]].
Last payment earns no interest because it's deposited at the end of the term.
Example: auto loan payments, bond interest.
Payments are made at the [[imp:beginning of each period]].
Each payment earns interest for one extra period compared to ordinary annuity.
Example: rent, life insurance premiums.
Start with $0.
For each period: multiply previous balance by (1 + i), then add the payment.
$$\text{New Balance} = (\text{Old Balance} \times (1 + i)) + \text{Payment}$$
Last payment earns no interest.

back: Year 1: $1,000 (no interest).
cards.front: Calculate the FV of $1,000 deposits at the end of each year for 2 years at 5% manually.

back: 1. Determine i (periodic rate) and n (number of payments).
2. Find the table factor at the intersection of n (row) and i (column).
3. Multiply the payment by the factor.
$$FV = \text{Payment} \times \text{Table Factor}$$
cards.front: How do you use an [[kw:ordinary annuity future value table]]?
Using a table, what is the FV of $500 deposited at the end of each year for 3 years at 8% (factor 3.2464)?

back: Each payment occurs one period earlier, so it earns interest for one extra period.
The total accumulated interest is greater.
$$FV_{\text{due}} = FV_{\text{ordinary}} \times (1 + i)$$
cards.front: Why is the future value of an annuity due higher than that of an ordinary annuity?
How do you convert the FV of an ordinary annuity to an annuity due?
back: Multiply the ordinary annuity FV by (1 + i).
$$FV_{\text{due}} = FV_{\text{ordinary}} \times (1 + i)$$
This adds one extra period of compounding.

cards.front: Ordinary FV is $5,000 at i=6%. Find annuity due FV.
What is the blueprint for annuity future value problems?
back: 1. Understand: note payment amount, frequency, rate, timing (end/beginning).
2. Solve: find n and i, look up factor (or compute manually), compute FV, adjust if annuity due.
3. Conclude: state FV; verify total deposits + interest.
